useCase.name: Find a student or staff member from the header, from anywhere in the system

intent.name: search.global
intent.summary: Find a student or staff member by name or by a system-issued number, within the role and branch scope the session already carries. One step. The matches are reported; no profile is opened.

A set defined by a figure is a drill-through, not a search.

steps.note: The only step. record_type and include_inactive are omitted entirely unless the request asks for them; the API defaults them to All and false.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The minimum length, the row scope and the role's right to search at all are enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand. Nothing matching is not a failure — it is the answer (E2).
plan.atomicity: One step. No student or staff record is created, changed or deactivated. One thing is written: the audit entry recording the term searched (BR-9), so even a run that returns nothing leaves a record that the search happened. That entry is never editable and is not something the controller can undo.

operations.name: search.global
operations.purpose: Match a name or a system-issued number against student and staff records inside the actor's role and branch scope, and return up to twenty of them with the total.

parameters.name: q
parameters.notes: The name or number only — the span of the sentence that names the person, never the sentence itself. "Ahmed Raza ko dhoondo" gives q "Ahmed Raza" (PR-10). Passed exactly as given: never re-spelled, transliterated or translated (PR-11). Minimum 3 characters; trimmed, case- and accent-insensitive. Matches name, roll number, student ID and staff ID only (BR-3) — never a guardian's mobile, an address or a date of birth.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.notes: Only where the sentence names the type outright — "find the teacher Nadia" is Staff. A form of address is not a type: madam, sir and baji narrow nothing (PR-12). Omit otherwise; the API defaults to All. Narrowing is safe from a permissions view because it never widens what the role may see (BR-1), but a wrong narrowing still hides the person.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.notes: True only where the request states the person has gone — "chala gaya tha", "TC ho gaya", "left last year" (PR-13). Never set true to widen a search that returned nothing — see PR-3.

parameters.name: branch_scope
parameters.notes: The branches this role may reach. Never from the request, even where the request names a campus. Global search widens reach across modules, never across permissions (BR-1).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: The academic session held in controller context (academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Up to twenty matches, each carrying what it takes to tell two people apart, plus the full total.

fields.name: matches
fields.description: record_type, record_id, name, class_or_department, roll_or_staff_number, status, branch_name, is_inactive. record_type and branch_name must be reported with each match (BR-4, BR-10).

fields.name: total_count
fields.description: How many matched in total, which may exceed the number shown (BR-6).

fields.name: full_list_key
fields.description: The student or staff list carrying the same term, where the total exceeds twenty (A1).

fields.name: scope_note
fields.description: What was searched in words — "Johar Town branch", "All branches", "Grade 1 and 2". Reported with the results so an empty answer is readable.

errors.meaning: Fewer than three characters were submitted.
errors.written: Nothing. No search ran, so no audit entry either.
errors.note: On screen no search runs and the panel does not open. Ask for more of the name rather than searching on two letters.

errors.meaning: Nothing in scope matches the term.
errors.written: The audit entry for the term searched (BR-9).
errors.note: Message: "No student or staff member matches that." This is the answer, not a failure. Never retried with include_inactive true or a shortened term.

errors.meaning: The search took longer than 10 seconds and was abandoned.
errors.written: Nothing reliable. The audit entry may or may not have been written.
errors.note: Message: "Search is taking longer than usual. Try a fuller name or a roll number." Report it; do not silently retry.

errors.meaning: The role may not use global search at all — Teacher, Student, Parent / Guardian and Driver.
errors.note: On screen the search box is not rendered in the header. A Teacher reaches their students through their class lists, which is the narrower and safer path.

operations.writesOnRead: Every search writes one audit entry naming the actor, the term and the time (BR-9), because this feature reaches personal data across the whole school. The entry recording which record was opened is written by whichever use case opens it, not by this plan.

planningRules.rule: Never chain a profile open onto this search, not even where exactly one record matches. A single result is reported for the actor to confirm, never opened for them (A2). The plan ends at the matches.
branch_scope comes from $session. A request naming a campus outside the actor's scope does not widen the search — it returns nothing, and that is correct. Never pass a branch from the request.

Never re-emit the search with include_inactive set true because it returned nothing. Inactive records are included only where the request asks for a former, left or struck-off person. A struck-off student surfacing unasked is how one gets mistaken for an enrolled one.
Never shorten, generalise or re-spell the term to find something. A search that matches nothing is the answer (E2), and a broadened one returns people nobody asked about.

Never put a guardian's mobile, an address, a date of birth or a parent's name in q. Only names and system-issued identifiers are matched (BR-3), and the use case's own open question records that a guardian's number has not been agreed as matchable.
Never plan this to enumerate. A term built to sweep a class, a department or a whole branch — "Grade 5", "Khan" to list every Khan — is a list, and lists are out of scope here.

Report each match with its record_type, and with branch_name where the scope spans branches. Dropping either is exactly how a student and a staff member of the same name, or two pupils of the same name at two campuses, get confused.
Where total_count exceeds shown_count, say so and offer the full list. Presenting twenty of sixty as the answer is a wrong answer.
Never emit this step to check whether a person exists before some other action. The audit log records every term searched, and a search run to probe is a search that will be read back later as one.

Put into q only the span that names the person, never the sentence around it. "Ahmed Raza ko dhoondo" searches for "Ahmed Raza"; ko dhoondo is grammar. A sentence passed whole matches nothing and reads afterwards, in the audit log, as a search nobody would have typed.

Never re-spell, transliterate or translate a name or a system-issued identifier. The record holds the spelling it was registered with, in Latin script, and Ayesha, Aisha and Ayeshah are three different searches. Where a name arrives in Urdu script, ask for it as it appears on the record rather than rendering it into Latin — a rendering is a guess with a person's identity in it. Eastern Arabic digits inside an identifier are normalised to Latin digits, which changes the script and not the number.

Set record_type only where the sentence names the type outright. Ustaad, sir, madam and baji are forms of address as often as they are job descriptions, and a wrong narrowing hides the person being looked for. Where it is not stated plainly, omit record_type and let All match — the record type comes back on every row anyway.

Read include_inactive from what the request states, not from how it is phrased. "Chala gaya tha", "TC ho gaya" and "left last year" all state that the person has gone; a wistful past tense does not. Where it is unclear, leave the flag off and report that nothing matched — PR-3 already forbids widening it afterwards.

reversal.statement: A search creates, changes and deactivates nothing, so there is nothing to reverse. The audit entry it writes is deliberate and never editable under the audit-trail convention — the controller must not attempt to remove or amend it.

request.text: counter pe ek parent khara hai, roll number 2024-0417 bata raha hai — ye kaun hai?
request.gloss: a parent at the counter is quoting roll number 2024-0417 — who is this?

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, academic session 2025-26.

steps.note: record_type and include_inactive are omitted entirely — the request asked for neither, so the API defaults them to All and false.

resolvedPlans.outcome: One match: Ayesha Khan, Student, Grade 4 Section B, roll 2024-0417, status Enrolled. It is reported, not opened — the actor confirms the person before a profile is loaded (AC-1, A2). One audit entry records the term.

steps.note: q is "ahmed raza" — the name lifted out of the sentence. ko dhoondo is grammar and never reaches the API (PR-10).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Two matches, one Student in Grade 7 Section A and one Staff member in Mathematics, each carrying its record type so the two are not confused (AC-2). Both are reported; neither is opened.

request.text: Bilal Khan ko dhoondo — mera khayal hai wo pichle saal chala gaya tha
request.gloss: find Bilal Khan — I think he left last year

steps.note: include_inactive is true because the request said he left — not because a first search came back empty (PR-3). record_type is Student because the request said so.

resolvedPlans.outcome: One match: Bilal Khan, Student, Grade 6 Section A as at leaving, status Left, marked as inactive (AC-3). Reported with that marking, so he is never taken for an enrolled pupil.
